summary: Transient GPU lease contention (thundering-herd) leading to p99 throughput collapse in dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary:
During a short burst of higher-priority requests from Veridian Analytics at ~2026-03-13T15:04:00Z, dedicated pool 'veridian-dedicated-usw2' experienced a sharp p99 throughput collapse (approx 4x increase in p99 latency and 60% drop in throughput) lasting ~11 minutes. Behavior appears correlated with a sudden flurry of small, concurrent allocation requests which caused the GPU allocator to briefly serialize lease grants and trigger backpressure into the autoscaler.

Impact:
- Veridian reported elevated inference latency and increased request timeouts impacting their reconciliation pipeline.
- Orders of magnitude increase in queuing seen on per-tenant queues.
- Customer-visible errors: 504 / timeout retries and elevated p99 token latency.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: veridian-dedicated-usw2 (reserved capacity: 8 x A100-40GB equiv)
- Cluster autoscaler: dedicated-autoscaler-v3 (policy: scale-by-demand with 30s evaluation window)
- Serving runtime: 2026.02.28 (commit 9a1f3bc)
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate a burst of 1200 concurrent short (<300ms service time) requests targeting small-batch routes
2) Ensure requests target gptx-13b-quantized and embedding-compact-v2 routes in same tenant
3) Observe allocator behavior: simultaneous lease requests, transient serialization, and scheduler queue spikes
4) Reproduce observed p99 spike within 1-2 minutes of burst start
logs_and_metrics: Metric snapshot (15:04-15:15 UTC): tenant_queue_length +420%, allocator_lease_latency 3x baseline, scheduler_backlog increased from 20->480, p99 token latency 4x
Serving runtime logs: repeated 'LeaseGrant: waiting for GPU free slot' messages (svc-runtime.log lines 14122-14178)
NVIDIA metrics during window: several GPUs transiently at 95-100% mem usage with low GPU util (~10-15% compute) indicating memory-hogging kernels from different tenant tasks
Cluster events: 15:06 autoscaler attempted to add 2 nodes but nodes joined after 2m 30s (beyond scale-up SLO)
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-13T15:22Z: Customer reported timeouts and a queueing alert. Asked for request IDs and sample traces. Escalating to SRE due to dedicated pool behavior.
Marco Chen (SRE) 2026-03-13T15:35Z: Noted pattern consistent with simultaneous short-lived allocations. Pulling allocator/debug logs and GPU process lists. Assigning to infra and runtime owners.
Evelyn Ross (Infra) 2026-03-13T16:05Z: Found pod churn and repeated lease contention logs. Opening related PR to add jitter to lease acquisition (infra#1892).
Veridian Ops (customer) 2026-03-13T16:30Z: Confirmed issue affected their reconciliation job; they reduced concurrency as a temporary mitigation. Asked for ETA on permanent fix.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Thundering-herd on GPU lease acquisition — many short requests cause allocator to repeatedly serialize access to certain GPU memory regions, creating head-of-line blocking.

Hypothesis 2: Noisy neighbor with memory-pinned kernels — other tenants running memory-heavy preprocessing tasks caused GPUs to appear 'full' (memory pressure) but with low compute, blocking new model allocations.

Evidence: nvidia-smi process list shows uncharacteristic persistent CUDA memory reservations by non-veridian pods at the same time; serving-runtime logs show repeated allocation retries with exponential backoff starting 15:04:07Z.
Observed autoscaler lag: scale-up latency exceeded expected window (2m 30s vs configured 30s) due to underlying cloud ASG throttling and slow node registration, exacerbating the impact.

Temporary mitigation applied at 15:40Z: instructed customer to shift to fallback smaller model (embedding-compact-v2) and throttle concurrent requests. Customer reported restored steady-state within 6 minutes of mitigation.

Relevant traces: https://observability.redwood.ai/trace/7f2b1c (shows lease wait spikes), dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/allocator/lease-latency?orgId=1&from=2026-03-13T15:00:00Z&to=2026-03-13T15:20:00Z
root_cause: A combination of short-lived concurrent allocation (thundering-herd) and a noisy-tenant performing memory-pinned preprocessing resulted in serialized GPU lease grants. The allocator's current lease acquisition path lacked jitter and had an atomic contention point; autoscaler scale-up latency and cloud node registration delays lengthened the outage window.
resolution_summary: Applied short-term customer mitigations (reduced concurrency, fallback model) and deployed immediate config changes to infra: added randomized jitter to GPU lease acquisition path, increased allocator internal timeout logging, and updated autoscaler to prefer warm spare nodes for dedicated pools. Patches deployed: infra PR #1892 (jitter), serving-runtime PR #847 (backoff tuning).
resolution_details: 15:50Z - Rolled infra PR #1892 (jitter on lease acquisition) to staging; observed allocator_lease_latency drop of ~60% in canary tests.
16:10Z - Rolled serving-runtime PR #847 with tuned backoff/retry behavior for allocations; reduced denial/retry storms in synthetic tests.
16:45Z - Adjusted autoscaler policy for dedicated pools to maintain 1 warm spare node when average queue_length > 50 for a tenant.
Customer updated to retry policy v2 and confirmed throughput recovered to expected levels after 6 minutes post-mitigation.
follow_up_actions: Owner: Marco Chen (SRE) - Monitor veridian-dedicated-usw2 for 72 hours after change; escalate if p99 regression recurs.
Owner: Evelyn Ross (Infra) - Implement long-term allocator redesign to remove global lease serialization point (RFC due 2026-04-03).
Owner: Product/Platform - Add tenant isolation warning in Console when memory-hogging workloads are detected in shared dedicated pools.
Owner: Support - Reach out to Veridian success manager with post-incident summary and recommend client-side concurrency controls and SDK exponential jitter (due 2026-03-16).
final_status_notes: Patch chain deployed and mitigations accepted by customer; monitoring window initiated. Incident remains In Progress until 72-hour monitoring completes and allocator redesign RFC is scheduled.
